studies.Population: Men aged 55–74 years enrolled in the PLCO cohort
studies.Reference: Higher insoluble fiber intake is associated with a lower risk of prostate cancer: results from the PLCO cohort.
studies.Authors: Shen Y, Yuan Q, Shi M, Luo B
studies.Timing: Prospective dietary assessment and follow-up for incident prostate cancer
studies.comparison_type: Highest quartile (Q4) versus lowest quartile (Q1) of soluble fiber intake

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 54,336 participants in the United States, consisting of 6,414 patients with PCa, were included in this study.

cases.excerpt: Therefore, this study examined the relationship between fiber intake and the risk of PCa by using data from Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial. A total of 54,336 participants in the United States, consisting of 6,414 patients with PCa, were included in this study.

effect_size.excerpt: Compared with individuals in the lowest quartile, individuals in the highest quartile of insoluble fiber intake had a significantly lower risk of PCa (aHR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.78-0.98). By contrast, no significant associations were detected between total fiber intake (aHR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.80-1.01) or soluble fiber intake (aHR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.80-1.02).

confidence_interval.excerpt: By contrast, no significant associations were detected between total fiber intake (aHR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.80-1.01) or soluble fiber intake (aHR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.80-1.02).

p_value.excerpt: Total fiber intake (Q4 vs. Q1: aHR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.80–1.01; P = 0.073) and soluble fiber intake (Q4 vs. Q1: aHR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.80–1.02; P = 0.086) were slightly lower but not significantly associated with the risk of PCa.

studies.Journal: Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics
studies.Timing: enrolled between 1993 and 2001; aged 55 to 74 years
studies.comparison_type: high versus low tertile soluble fiber intake

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: A total of 49 476 participants (annual screening arm: 25 669 men; usual care arm: 23 807 men) aged 55 to 74 years were enrolled from the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Study between the years 1993 and 2001.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Compared with the low tertile total fiber intake, high tertile total fiber intake in the annual screening arm was linked to reduced prostate cancer risk (adjusted hazard ratio 0.87; 95% CI, 0.76 to 0.99), and high-soluble fiber intake in the usual care arm had a similar association (adjusted hazard ratio 0.86; 95% CI, 0.75 to 0.98) after adjusting for confounders.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.9 (95% CI: 0.83–0.98), suggesting that soluble dietary fiber intake is associated with a lower risk of prostate cancer. These findings were supported by low between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.
